speaker: Basil
current_text: Psst. Hello. I'm Basil, line cook. Ladle in one hand, nerves in the other. We Gourmands feed the kingdom and protect it. Every plate is a promise. Every golem is a guard.

speaker: Basil
current_text: Ten years ago {villain}'s people came to the Buffet, and the Grand Chef... changed. Chef ALWAYS tastes, and this Chef doesn't. She just smiles at the soup.

speaker: Basil
current_text: She put the Special Sauce in every pot. Our rules: nobody leaves hungry, nobody double-dips, and we say "Yes, Chef." Quietly. Nobody asks about the Test Kitchen. I'm not asking.

speaker: Basil
current_text: It wasn't her. It was a Doppelganger, wearing her face for ten years, and you walked right up to it. I'd have fainted. I did faint, earlier, about something else.

speaker: Basil
current_text: The real Chef is back in her own kitchen, tasting her own soup. We all cried. Say it with me: Yes, Chef. Louder. YES, CHEF! ...Oh, that felt good. We mean it this time.

speaker: Basil
current_text: She remembered the cake. The very first thing she said when we opened the freezer was "Is the boy all right?" I didn't know what to tell her.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
current_text: Oh! A customer! A helper! A pair of hands! Sous-Chef Tarragon, fetcher of things. I fetch. All day. My legs have their own legs now.
new_text: Sous-Chef Tarragon, fetcher of things - oh, good, more hands! I've been running all day and still haven't caught up with lunch.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
current_text: We're always out of something. Honey, basil, ghost pepper... half our deliveries go to the Test Kitchen, and nothing comes back. I once fetched a whole pig. Wrong pig. It's still angry.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
current_text: Don't tell the Grand Chef I said anything. She hears everything. She just never tastes anything.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
current_text: Any ingredients? Anything? I'll take a single leaf of anything.
new_text: Ingredients, please, anything? I'm one leaf away from calling this a salad and going home.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
current_text: I'm not proud. I'm hungry. And a bit scared. Mostly hungry.
new_text: I'm hungry and a bit scared. If either came with a side dish, we'd be sorted.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
current_text: Tarragon! Sous-Chef! Free!

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
current_text: The ingredients are coming back from the Test Kitchen by the cartload. Pigs, even. Not the angry pig. A different one. A happy one.
new_text: Ingredients are coming back from the Test Kitchen by the cartload, even pigs! A happy pig this time; I've had enough professional disagreements.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
current_text: Fetching is fun again! Everyone waves at me! Nobody asks me to fetch cannonballs!
new_text: People wave when I fetch things now! And nobody asks for cannonballs - I prefer a lighter lunch.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
current_text: Madame Mirepoix. Dessert dealer and card shark of the Grand Pantry. Tonight's tasting menu: three cards, lightly foiled, served with disdain.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
current_text: Everything here is Gourmand-issue and, as of this year, inspected by the Test Kitchen. The stamp is on the cake. The cake, darling, is for decoration.
new_text: Gourmand-issue, inspected by the Test Kitchen as of this year. The stamp is on the decorative cake, which has never looked more unappetizing.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
current_text: I take gold, favours and sprinkles, in that order. I do not take the Special Sauce. I have been pretending to eat it for months.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
current_text: Back again, darling? The cards are plated. The cake is for decoration. The sauce is for other people.
new_text: Your cards are plated, darling; the cake is decorative. As for the Special Sauce, I recommend the air beside it.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
current_text: Madame Mirepoix, free of the sauce. My taste buds came back last week, and darling... the sugar. I wept into a meringue.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
current_text: Cakes by day, cards by night. All by appointment, and all by choice.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
current_text: Sit down, darling. Have a slice. The cake is for eating now. I checked.
new_text: Sit down and have a slice, darling. The cake has been promoted from decoration to dessert.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
current_text: You can fetch? Wonderful! We need three ingredients, quick. Our stolen deliveries are scattered all over the Buffet: truffle by the broccoli, salt by the river, honey up the Butte.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
current_text: Pick up any three and come back. I'll make it worth your while. I'm begging with my whole apron.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
current_text: Three ingredients, any three, from around the Buffet. The pantry is empty and somebody is staring at me. Please hurry.
new_text: Bring any three ingredients from around the Buffet. The pantry is empty, and I can't keep calling that a minimalist menu.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
current_text: Three whole ingredients! The Pantry is saved! For today!

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
current_text: Here, a little something. It's a card. It's soup. It's soup you can play.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
current_text: The pantry is stocked. Until tomorrow. Then we start over. It's a lovely cycle. I'm fine.
new_text: The pantry's stocked until tomorrow, when we do it all again. Fetching has a wonderful sense of repetition; I'd like to send it back.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
current_text: A favour, darling. A customer of mine wants a Hearty Pot Pie, a real one, and the Grand Oven is sulking. It keeps being asked to cook prototypes.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
current_text: Bake one for me: honey, giant basil and a ghost pepper, into the Grand Oven by the arch, then bring it here. Careful with the pepper. It is not a team player.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
current_text: One Hearty Pot Pie, darling. Honey, basil and a ghost pepper into the Grand Oven by the arch. I shall wait. I have cake.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
current_text: A pie. A real one, golden and warm. My customer is going to cry.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
current_text: I am going to cry. Discreetly. Here is your reward, you scrappy little thing. Thank you.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
current_text: The best pie this Pantry has seen in years. The oven would like a word with you. I believe it wants to say thank you.

speaker: Basil
current_text: Um. A word? Quietly? Old Meatloaf, our oldest golem, has stopped working. The Test Kitchen tried to strip him for parts. We got him back in two pieces. He hasn't spoken since Tuesday.

speaker: Basil
current_text: He needs sea salt for his joints and a black truffle for his heart, both out in the Buffet. Mend him and Sir Loin will let you through the Layer-Cake Town gate. Yes, Chef? ...Please?

speaker: Basil
current_text: Old Meatloaf is over by the west wall of the Grand Pantry. Sea salt, a black truffle, and a bit of tenderness.

speaker: Basil
current_text: He's walking! He's sizzling! Old Meatloaf is back on duty! I'm not crying. I'm standing near onions.

speaker: Basil
current_text: Here's your reward, and Sir Loin will open his gate for you now. Well done. Yes, Chef.

speaker: Basil
current_text: Old Meatloaf is the best golem in the kingdom. Don't tell the others. They know.

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
current_text: You season Old Meatloaf's joints with the sea salt and tuck the black truffle where his heart should be. He sits up slowly.

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
current_text: "...Chef?" he says. "Yes, Chef," you say, because it feels right. His eyes uncross.

speaker: Professor Pate
current_text: Answer well and earn gold, glory and the respect of a very old book. Answer poorly and earn a gentle, scholarly sigh, lightly salted.

speaker: Professor Pate

speaker: Professor Pate

speaker: Professor Pate

speaker: Professor Pate
current_text: One. A pinch of knowledge, barely seasoned. Here is a small token. It is a thimble of encouragement.

speaker: Professor Pate
current_text: Two. Half-baked. A fine place to start. Half-baked things can still be rescued.

speaker: Professor Pate
current_text: Three! Nearly perfect. Perfect would make me suspicious. Take your reward and a warm roll.

speaker: Professor Pate
current_text: FOUR! A perfectly risen set! You may now call yourself a Certified Gourmand, First Class.

speaker: Professor Pate
current_text: The reward is real. The certificate is imaginary.

speaker: Professor Pate
current_text: Another round! The Cookbook pays a small fee for repeat scholarship.

speaker: Professor Pate
current_text: Not a pass. Wrong, but deliciously wrong. Walk the Endless Buffet, read the signs, and come back. There is no limit on attempts.
